## 1. Request

- PLAN: `cpt-{system}-plan-{slug}`
- Literature mode: {`allowed` | `blind`, copied from the PLAN's section 2. A PLAN whose mode is `none` produces no LITERATURE.}
- Exclusions checked: {under `blind`, the number of rows of the PLAN's Excluded table; the gate fails if it differs from the PLAN's row count. `not applicable` under `allowed`.}
- Strategy: {`related` | `review` | `metareview` | `scout`}
- Anchor: {DOI, id, title or draft; or Subject: the subject with its must-have terms}
- Bounds: {years, excluded fields, open access only; for scout the quantity, unit and required conditions}
- Depth: {quick | deep}
- Output shape: {…}
- Cost stated before running: {OpenAlex credits, Consensus calls}
- Cost used: {per source, retrieval and the online gate's DOI lookups, and the total against the stated cost}

## 2. Sources

{One row per source that ran, with the canonical query so a person can rerun it; one row per source that was configured but skipped, with the reason; one row per source not configured. Nothing substituted silently.}

| source | ran | query or tool calls | budget used | note |
|--------|-----|---------------------|-------------|------|
| OpenAlex | yes / no | {canonical query URL} | {credits} | {…} |
| Consensus | yes / no / not configured | {query, filters, page_size} | {calls} | {plan} |
| Hypothesis | yes / no / not configured | {collection id, tools} | — | {coverage, see section 4} |

- Removed by exclusion: {under `blind`, the number of retrieved papers removed from the Set because they matched an item of the PLAN's Excluded table: the count only, never the matched DOI, title, term, benchmark or author; `not applicable` under `allowed`.}

## 3. Set

{Every paper the analysis may cite, one line each. Role: reference / citer / related / same-topic (Path 1); anchor / snowball / group member (Path 2); review (Path 3); candidate (Path 4). Resolved: `yes` | `unresolved` | `no DOI`; `yes` when the DOI returned a record from OpenAlex on this run, `no DOI` with the DOI cell `—`. Approved by: the person who approved the set and the date (P12). A paper not in this table is not cited anywhere below. Under `blind` no row matches an excluded item.}

| # | DOI | year | title | role | cited by | resolved | OA link |
|---|-----|------|-------|------|----------|----------|---------|

- Approved by: {person, YYYY-MM-DD}

## 4. Collection

{Only when Hypothesis ran. Collection id and name; coverage as `k of N`: papers of the approved set indexed in the collection over papers in the approved set; the DOIs the collection lacks; index date. A claims map built on a collection that holds less than half the approved set is a map of the uploads, not of the subject, and the gate refuses `verified`. Write `not used` otherwise.}

## 5. Analysis

{Path 1: the prior work grouped by sub-problem — what was established, by whom, with which method, and what the anchor adds. Path 2: one block per group (authors, institutions, approach, data, years active, achievements in the Set's own terms, assessment: succeeding / stalled / too early, with evidence), then the cross-group observations. Path 3: per review its scope, period, trends and gaps; then trends asserted by several reviews, trends contradicted between reviews, what no review covers; no primary-source claims. Path 4: the scout table `paper | doi | link | what_measured | how_measured | constraints | value | unit | passage`, one row per measurement, with constraints in the paper's words and units copied, never converted; the same rows are written as CSV beside this artifact. Its values are claims, not data: they reach a PLAN only through section 6 and never become a DATASET.

Every sentence that asserts something about a paper ends with its Set row number in brackets. The request's anchor is named without a row number; every other paper is cited by Set row. A paper not in the Set may not be mentioned.}

## 6. Claims

{Each claim the PLAN may use. Claims row n is the n-th data row of the Claims table, counted from 1 in table order; rows are never reordered or deleted after a PLAN cites them. Citations read `<LITERATURE ID>, claim n`. Quote: the paper's words; for a scout value, the passage it came from. Location: section and paragraph, or page, where the quote was found on this run. Status: `verified` when the row's Set `resolved` cell is `yes` and the quote was located; `assumed` otherwise. An assumed claim may motivate a diagnostic batch, never a parameter range or a mechanism (P10). A row enters the PLAN's section 2 only after a person approves it (P12).}

| claim | set # | quote | location | status |
|-------|-------|-------|----------|--------|

## 7. Candidate Hypotheses

{Where the Set contradicts itself — two groups, two reviews, two measurements that disagree — one candidate per contradiction, as a proposed row for the PLAN's Hypothesis Space: mechanism or effect, the claims it rests on (cited as `<LITERATURE ID>, claim n`), a proposed diagnostic condition, status NOT YET TESTED. Proposed, never confirmed: the human confirms it in the PLAN. Write `none` if the Set is consistent.}

| candidate | claims | proposed diagnostic condition | status |
|-----------|--------|-------------------------------|--------|

## 8. Attestation

{One bullet per line, in these forms; the gate matches the labels `Retrieval:`, `Set approved by` and `Gate, offline:` / `Gate, online:`.
- Retrieval: `<lit_run invocation>`, run <YYYY-MM-DD>; {lit_run.py version, sources and endpoints, requests, cost}
- Set approved by <person>, <YYYY-MM-DD>.
- Hand-over to `<PLAN ID>` section 2: {claims n, …, each `verified` or `assumed`}; approved by <person>, <YYYY-MM-DD>.
- Gate, offline|online: `<invocation exactly as run>`, run <YYYY-MM-DD>: PASS|FAIL; {DOIs looked up, credits, notes}
One gate line per invocation. The label `online` requires `--resolve` and `--plan` in the invocation; any other invocation is `offline`. Status `verified` needs an `online` PASS (L9).}
